I’m the CEO of Product Hunt and see 100s of launches a week. My current thoughts on new infra begging for startups: 

1) Voice AI - infra for voice agents is getting really good w @pipecat_ai @Vapi_AI @DeepgramAI @ElevenLabs et al. and yet I rarely see good voice tech in the real world. 

2) Decision Models - Jev / @typesafeai leading the charge. It reminds me of the mech-building in Zelda TOTK - an explosion of possibilities!

3) Personal Agents - they work now. And they need tools, apps, MCPs.

4) Extensions (OpenAI). We all live in agentic interfaces now. It’s like a new platform. Someone needs to build a Slack replacement that lives in Codex, for example.

candidates.text:
I remember touching 120km/hr on the Leh Srinagar highway. Remember Anna shouting “Bhai Bhaiiii” “Saum sambhaal ke”

It was a Royal enfield classic. I’d waited all my life to drive an enfield in Ladakh.

I remember it vividly. Taking a turn, seeing a truck in the center of the road coming down as I was going up. I’d been driving bikes before my feet could touch the ground. I knew we were gonna crash.

There was a ditch on the left and the mountain on the right. Anna saw the truck then and with a lot of faith said “Saum truckkkkk” 

It’s not even funny how the world slows down in such situations. I decided that even if the truck hit us bang on, we’d probably just get pushed back hard but won’t go in the ditch.

I started applying the brakes. I could see the truck slowing down. We were headed to collide. And just then Anna jumped off the bike. Only then it hit me that this was an option too but I’d committed to applying the brakes.

When we did collide head on I felt like a wave went through my body. I just kept pressing the brake with all my might and stood ground. The bike dragged along with the truck for about 50 meters.

When it was over. The truck stopped. My first instinct in such an incident, like any legitimate Kanpur boy, is to beat the shit out of the other driver.

This time, however, I remember feeling calm. Like I’d been reborn. I felt like it was over and I’d seen death.

The enfield was such a beast though and took it like nothing happened. Midway it gave up. A monk took us to a nearby army camp that towed the bike for us and took us in.

When the night ended, I felt a renewed sense of gratitude for everything I had in my life. I’d become too caught up in work. I was spending close to 0 time with family or my then girlfriend now wife.

The next day, we paid damages and got a new bike. Anna asked if I’ll be comfortable driving. I took the keys and drove us over the highest motorable road in the world.

That trip shifted something in me that’s difficult to explain. I stopped caring about promotions and titles and became more intentional, fearless, and risk taking.

Next year, in August, it’ll be 10 years since the trip. And I can’t wait to go back.
